instructions: Pull the meat off the rotisserie chicken, leaving the skin behind, and chop it. That should be about 3 cups.
Dice a quarter of the red onion and the 2 celery stalks, chop 3 tbsp of the parsley, and halve the grapes.
In a large bowl, whisk together the mayonnaise, mustard, 2 tbsp lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Add the chicken, onion, celery, 2 tbsp of the parsley and the grapes, and stir until everything is coated.
Halve the avocados and remove the pits. Scoop about 2 spoonfuls out of each half, leaving a cup. Chop what you scooped out and stir it into the chicken salad.
Fill each avocado half with a large spoonful of the chicken salad and sprinkle with the last 1 tbsp parsley. Serve right away.
To make it ahead, stop after the chicken salad and keep it in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days. Fill the avocados right before you eat.
method_notes: Food Republic is the lead (4.9 out of 5 from 33 ratings) and the other versions (Cookin' with Mima, Hunker) agree on chicken, mayonnaise, celery, onion and parsley piled into avocado halves; they differ in the yogurt, nuts, grapes and cranberries. This follows the lead, scaled to 3 cups of chicken. Greek yogurt is replaced with a little more mayonnaise to keep it dairy-free, and the walnuts are left out for nut-free. The avocado is left in its skin, as the other versions do.
